'''Taurean Waller-Prince''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|ɔr|i|ə|n}} {{respell|TOR|ee|ən}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born March 22, 1994)<ref>{{cite web|title=Taurean Prince Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/princta02.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 8, 2020}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor Bears]]. He was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 12th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]], but his draft rights were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Prince played three seasons for the Hawks before being traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in 2019. He has also played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

==High school career==
Prince played three seasons of high school basketball under head coach Jim Weaver at [[Earl Warren High School]] in [[San Antonio]], Texas. As a senior, he led the team to the state semifinals. He originally chose to play [[college basketball]] with the [[LIU Sharks men's basketball|LIU Brooklyn Blackbirds]], but switched to [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] due to a coaching change within the former program.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taurean_prince_821205.html|title=Taurean Prince bio|work=BaylorBears.com|access-date=August 6, 2015|archive-date=June 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160626144841/http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taurean_prince_821205.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Prince played 24 games off the bench in his freshman season. He finished the year averaging 3.7 points and 2.2 rebounds in 6.4 minutes per game. In the spring prior to his sophomore season, Prince was on the [[Big 12 Conference]] Commissioner's Honor Roll. After averaging 6.2 points and 2.8 rebounds in 14.2 minutes per game and appearing in all 38 of [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]]'s games, he won the Big 12 Sixth Man Award and earned all-conference honors.<ref name=bio /> Entering his fourth season, [[Fran Fraschilla]] labeled him as a strong candidate for [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] in [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]].<ref name=panam>{{cite web|first=Ashley|last=Hodge|url=http://baylor.247sports.com/Bolt/Taurean-Waller-Prince-helps-lead-USA-to-bronze-medal-at-PanAm-38385209|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150726234601/http://baylor.247sports.com/Bolt/Taurean-Waller-Prince-helps-lead-USA-to-bronze-medal-at-PanAm-38385209|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 26, 2015|title=Taurean Waller-Prince helps lead USA to bronze medal at PanAm|work=247Sports.com|date=July 5, 2015|access-date=August 6, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Atlanta Hawks (2016–2019)===
On June 23, 2016, Prince was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 12th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on July 7 in a three-team deal also involving the [[Indiana Pacers]] the Jazz received [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]] and the Pacers received [[Jeff Teague]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Jessica |date=July 5, 2016 |title=Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To Taurean Prince |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-draft-rights-taurean-prince |access-date=July 5, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On July 15, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Jaryd |date=July 15, 2016 |title=Hawks Sign First Round Picks Taurean Prince & DeAndre' Bembry |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/features/hawks-sign-first-round-picks-taurean-prince-deandre-bembry |access-date=September 15, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 11, 2017, he had a then season-best 17 points in a 107–90 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900376|title=Prince scores 17 as Hawks rout Grizzlies 107-90|work=ESPN.com|date=March 11, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2017}}</ref> On April 6, he scored a career-high 20 points in a 123–116 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900555|title=Millsap, Hardaway boost Hawks past Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=April 6, 2017|access-date=April 6, 2017}}</ref> With 11 points in Game 4 of the Hawks' first-round playoff series against the [[Washington Wizards]], Prince became the first Hawks rookie to reach double-figures in his first four playoff games since [[Pete Maravich]] did it in five straight in 1971.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950425|title=Balanced Hawks hold off Wizards 111-101, even series 2-all|work=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2017|access-date=April 25, 2017}}</ref> During his rookie season, Prince had multiple assignments with the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA Development League]], pursuant to the flexible assignment rule.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
[[File:Taurean Prince (33599620765) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Prince with the Atlanta Hawks in 2017]]
On December 12, 2017, Prince scored a career-high 24 points in a 123–114 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975148|title=James scores 25 has 17 assists, as Cavs beat Hawks 123-114|work=ESPN.com|date=December 12, 2017|access-date=December 12, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he made a career-high five 3-pointers and had 17 points in a 96–94 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975176|title=Evans scores 22 to lead Grizzlies over Hawks, 96-94|work=ESPN.com|date=December 15, 2017|access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref> On December 29, he had a career-high 30 points and 10 rebounds in a 111–98 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Prince matched a career high with five 3-pointers and extended his career-high streak of games with at least one 3-pointer to 17.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975268|title=DeRozan scores 25 as Raptors beat Hawks 111-98|work=ESPN.com|date=December 29, 2017|access-date=December 29, 2017}}</ref> On February 2, 2018, he set a new career high with 31 points in a 119–110 loss to the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975513|title=Super sub: Rozier powers Celtics past Hawks, 119-110|work=ESPN.com|date=February 2, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2018}}</ref> On March 11, he set a new career high with 38 points in a 129–122 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975739|title=LaVine, Portis lead Bulls past short-handed Hawks, 129-122|work=ESPN.com|date=March 11, 2018|access-date=March 11, 2018}}</ref> Six days later, he had another 38-point effort in a 122–117 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975787|title=Giannis' double-double helps Bucks hold on to beat Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref> On April 8, he made seven of eight 3-pointers to score 33 points in a 112–106 win over the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975948|title=Prince scores 33, Hawks beat resting Celtics, win 112-106|work=ESPN.com|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=April 8, 2018}}</ref>

On October 19, in just the second game of the season, Prince scored a season-high 28 points against the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/princta02/gamelog/2019/|title=Taurean Waller-Prince 2018-19 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 4, 2019}}</ref> On January 13, 2019, against the Bucks, Prince returned to action after missing 18 games with a left ankle sprain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071316|title=Antetokounmpo leads the way, Bucks win Budenholzer's return|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2019|access-date=January 13, 2019}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2019–2021)===
On July 6, 2019, Prince, alongside a 2021 second-round pick, was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Allen Crabbe]], the draft rights to [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]], and a protected 2020 first-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sapp |first=Demetris |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Taurean Prince and 2021 Second Round Draft Pick From Atlanta |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/07/06/brooklyn-nets-acquire-taurean-prince-and-2021-second-round-draft-pick-atlanta |access-date=July 6, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 21, Prince, signed a two-year, $29 million contract extension with the Nets.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |author-link1=Adrian Wojnarowski |last2=Andrews |first2=Malika |author-link2=Malika Andrews |name-list-style=and |date=October 21, 2019 |title=Nets extend Taurean Prince on 2-year, $29 million deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27897757 |access-date=September 15, 2024 |website=ESPN}}</ref> He made his Nets debut two days later, recording 15 points, eleven rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 127–126 overtime loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mahoney |first=Brian |date=October 23, 2019 |title=IRVING SCORES 50 BUT MISSES LAST SHOT, WOLVES TOP NETS IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900006 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 1, Prince scored a season-high 27 points, alongside twelve rebounds, in a 123–116 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mahoney |first=Brian |date=November 1, 2019 |title=NETS SLOW DOWN HARDEN, ROCKETS IN 123-116 VICTORY |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900069 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In March 2020, the NBA season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. After the game on November 12, 2019, against the [[Utah Jazz]], Prince traded jerseys with former Baylor Bears teammate [[Royce O'Neale]]. In July, Prince tested positive for COVID-19 and sat out for the restart of the season in the [[NBA Bubble]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=July 7, 2020 |title=Sources: Nets' Taurean Prince declared out of restart after positive coronavirus test |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29425186 |access-date=September 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2021)===
On January 14, 2021, Prince and center [[Jarrett Allen]] were traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a multi-player, four-team deal with the [[Houston Rockets]] and [[Indiana Pacers]] that sent [[James Harden]] to Brooklyn.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire James Harden|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/01/14/brooklyn-nets-acquire-james-harden|website=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2021|access-date=January 14, 2021}}</ref> Prince made his Cavaliers debut on January 20, recording 17 points, seven rebounds and four assists in a 147–135 double-overtime win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Withers |first=Tom |date=January 21, 2021 |title=IRVING RETURNS, BUT NEW-LOOK NETS BEATEN BY CAVS IN 2 OTS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000216 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 14, he scored a season-high 25 points, alongside four rebounds and three assists, in a 103–90 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Steve |date=April 14, 2021 |title=ALLEN SCORES 15 IN RETURN, CAVALIERS BEAT HORNETS 103-90 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000829 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 27, Prince underwent a successful left ankle arthroscopic surgery after missing three games with left ankle soreness. The surgery subsequently ended his season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=April 28, 2021 |title=Taurean Prince Status Update |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/status-update-210428 |access-date=April 28, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2021–2023)===
On August 3, 2021, Prince, alongside a 2022 second-round pick and cash considerations, was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Ricky Rubio]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gold |first=Matthew |date=August 3, 2021 |title=Cavaliers Acquire Ricky Rubio from the Minnesota Timberwolves |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/rubio-trade-210803 |access-date=September 15, 2024 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Prince made his Timberwolves debut on October 20, recording five points, three rebounds and two assists in a 124–106 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=October 21, 2021 |title=EDWARDS ENERGIZES WOLVES IN OPENING 124-106 WIN OVER ROCKETS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100008 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 1, 2022, he scored a season-high 23 points, alongside nine rebounds, two assists and two steals, in a 130–115 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Brian |date=February 1, 2022 |title=WOLVES' BENCH LEADS THE WAY IN 130-115 WIN AGAINST NUGGETS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100770 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Two days later, Prince again scored 23 points, alongside six rebounds, in a 128–117 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2022 |title=EDWARDS, TOWNS LEAD TIMBERWOLVES PAST PISTONS, 128-117 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100782 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> After a [[NBA Play-In Tournament|play-in tournament]] win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], the Timberwolves qualified for the playoffs for the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]]. However, they fell to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in six games during the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=April 30, 2022 |title=GRIZZLIES RALLY AGAIN PAST WOLVES 114-106 TO REACH 2ND ROUND |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mem-vs-min-0042100156 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On June 30, 2022, Prince signed a two-year, $16 million contract extension with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=June 29, 2022 |title=Minnesota Timberwolves, Taurean Prince agree to 2-year, $16 million contract extension, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34163648 |access-date=June 30, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manzano |first=Francisco |date=June 30, 2022 |title=Timberwolves Sign Taurean Prince to Contract Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-taurean-prince-to-contract-extension |access-date=June 30, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2023–2024)===
On July 6, 2023, Prince signed a one-year, $4.5 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Taurean Prince |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-taurean-prince-070623 |access-date=July 6, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> On December 9, Prince and the Lakers won the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament|inaugural season]] of the [[NBA In-Season Tournament]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=2023-12-10 |title=Lakers win in-season tournament final behind Anthony Davis' 41-20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39080368 |access-date=2024-09-15 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He made 78 appearances (49 starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 8.9 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.

===Milwaukee Bucks (2024–2026)===
On July 9, 2024, Prince signed a minimum deal with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Taurean Prince|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-taurean-prince|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}}</ref> On December 17, Prince and the Bucks won the [[2024 NBA Cup]], which made Prince the first player in history to win multiple Cup titles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-18 |title=Bucks Beat Thunder to Win First NBA Cup, Giannis Antetokounmpo Named MVP |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/news/bucks-beat-thunder-to-win-first-nba-cup-giannis-antetokounmpo-named-mvp-ak1987 |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=Milwaukee Bucks On SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-12-18 |title=Taurean Prince makes NBA history with back-to-back titles |url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/nba/milwaukee-bucks/2024/12/18/67626f2d268e3e31398b45d5.html |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=MARCA |language=en}}</ref> He made 80 appearances (73 starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.9 assists.

On July 1, 2025, Prince re-signed with the Bucks on a two-year, $7.1 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Milwaukee Brewers set to re-sign forward Taurean Prince to two-year deal|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2025/06/30/milwaukee-bucks-set-to-resign-taurean-prince-on-free-agent-deal-two-year/84420654007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=z116751p119950c119950e005200v116751b0047xxd004765&gca-ft=125&gca-ds=sophi|access-date=October 28, 2025|website=jsonline.com|language=en}}</ref> On November 13, Prince suffered a [[herniated disc]] in his neck, and was ruled out indefinitely after undergoing surgery.<ref>{{cite web |date=10 November 2025 |title=Bucks veteran forward out long term with neck injury |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234746-bucks-taurean-prince-out-long-term-neck-injury.html |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 10, 2026, Prince made his return during a loss to the [[2025–26 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]] after being out for four months.<ref>[https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2026/03/10/milwaukee-bucks-taurean-prince-returned-to-play-after-four-months-neck-surgery/89019820007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z117241p119650l004450c119650e1197xxv117241d--55--b--55--&gca-ft=229&gca-ds=sophi Milwaukee Bucks' Taurean Prince returned to play after four months]</ref> On April 10, he recorded 18 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists in a 125–108 victory over the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bucks 125-108 Nets (Apr 10, 2026) Game Recap|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401811034|access-date=June 29, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2026–present)===
On July 8, 2026, Prince was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in a six-team trade.<ref>{{cite web |title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE JOHN COLLINS, TAUREAN PRINCE AND GARY HARRIS IN SIX-TEAM TRADE |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-john-collins-taurean-prince-and-gary-harris-in-six-team-trade |website=nba.com |publisher=NBA Media Ventures, LLC |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
In the summer of 2015, following his junior season, Prince helped the [[United States men's national basketball team]] win the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]]. He was on a team led by [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]] and [[Anthony Randolph]].<ref name=panam />

==Personal life==
On August 25, 2022, Prince was arrested on a "fugitive warrant-out-of-state extradite" at [[Miami International Airport]] on account of a "dangerous drugs" charge from Texas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |title=Timberwolves' Taurean Prince Arrested on Fugitive Warrant at Miami Airport |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10046682-timberwolves-taurean-prince-arrested-on-fugitive-warrant-at-miami-airport |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826022951/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10046682-timberwolves-taurean-prince-arrested-on-fugitive-warrant-at-miami-airport |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 26, 2022 |access-date=2022-08-26 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> On November 19, 2022, it was announced that Prince would not face charges despite the arrest.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2022 |title=NBA's Taurean Prince Won't Face Charges Over Drug Arrest |url=https://www.tmz.com/2022/11/19/nba-taurean-prince-wont-face-charges-over-drug-arrest/ |access-date=September 15, 2024 |website=TMZ}}</ref>

Prince is a [[Muslim]] and talked about fasting for Ramadan in a post-game interview.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRh34uXad74 |title=Taurean Prince walk-off interview after the Lakers win over the Cavaliers. |language=en |access-date=2024-04-19 |via=youtube.com}}</ref>

Prince honored his mother, Tamiyko, by wearing her maiden name, Waller, on the back of his jersey as Waller-Prince while playing for the Baylor Bears.<ref>{{cite web |last=Werner |first=John |title=Taurean Prince's tough upbringing gave him unique perspective on court |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/taurean-prince-s-tough-upbringing-gave-him-unique-perspective-on-court/article_404b7e2a-7317-579f-80c9-c5a534d3449e.html |website=Waco Tribune-Herald |access-date=April 22, 2024 |date=March 5, 2016}}</ref>
